output:
I'll start by looking at the docs and the package layout.

The last call was cut off before it ran. I'll apply the fixes in smaller steps, starting with the lexer.

That call was cut off again. I'll use `edit_file` for the next changes, one file at a time.

The shell call was truncated again. I'll write the edge-case script to a file first, then run it.

I fixed the `layercfg` package to follow the docs, and all 56 unit tests now pass with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. `tools/check.py` reports 0 broken on all four rules. It resolves 136 of the 150 configs in `/app/data`. The other 14 are refused with errors that match what the docs require, for example bad bool or duration text, a reference cycle, a missing shared file and an unknown escape.

I also ran a few edge cases by hand (`5ms`, `1.5KiB`, `a, b,, c ,`, the `#` comment forms, `:` before `=`, continuations) and they came out as the docs say. I did not touch `/app/tests`, `/app/data` or `/app/docs`, and I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

What I changed, by file:
- **`lexer.py`:**
  - The separator is now whichever of `=` or `:` comes first.
  - Section headers and `%include` lines allow only spaces and tabs as whitespace.
  - Stripping of lines and keys is limited to spaces and tabs.
- **`values.py`:**
  - An inline `#` only starts a comment when it follows a space or tab.
  - `\$` in a double-quoted value now gives `$$`.
  - Stripping of quoted and unquoted values is limited to spaces and tabs.
- **`interp.py`:**
  - References are now expanded after the whole config is merged, so they see the final value of each key. Before, each value was expanded as its line was read.
  - A dotted reference splits at the last dot.
- **`loader.py`:**
  - After a shared file ends, the including file goes on in the section it was in before the `%include`.
  - Each shared file appears once in `includes`, in the order it was first read.
- **`report.py`:** Template sections (names starting with `_`) are no longer written or converted.
- **`convert.py`:**
  - `ms` is now read as milliseconds rather than minutes followed by `s`.
  - `KB`, `MB`, `GB` and `TB` are powers of 1000.
  - List items are trimmed and empty ones dropped.
  - Trimming is limited to spaces and tabs.
- **`data.py`:** Files are read as raw UTF-8 bytes so Python doesn't turn a lone `\r` into a line break, which the docs don't allow.

One ambiguity I left alone: a config's lines are split first and its values are parsed as each line is applied. A config with both a bad value and a bad `%include` therefore reports whichever comes first in the file. The docs don't say which error should win in that case.

command_result.command: cd /app && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | head -100 && cat docs/overview.md && wc -l layercfg/*.py docs/*
cd /app && cat docs/syntax.md docs/include.md docs/interp.md docs/types.md docs/output.md docs/changelog.md; ls docs/archive tools data | head -30
cd /app && for f in layercfg/*.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done
cd /app && sed -n 40,70p docs/include.md; cat docs/interp.md; sed -n 1,12p docs/types.md; cat docs/archive/*; cat layercfg/interp.py; sed -n 1,35p layercfg/lexer.py
cd /app && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -60; cat tools/check.py | head -60; ls tests/expected; ls data/configs | wc -l

cd /app && python - <<'EOF'
import re
p='layercfg/lexer.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''SECTION = re.compile(r"\\[\\s*(" + NAME + r")\\s*\\](?:\\s+[#;].*)?")''','''SECTION = re.compile(r"\\[[ \\t]*(" + NAME + r")[ \\t]*\\](?:[ \\t]+[#;].*)?")''')
s=s.replace('''INCLUDE = re.compile(r"%include\\s+([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\.conf)(?:\\s+#.*)?")''','''INCLUDE = re.compile(r"%include[ \\t]+([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\.conf)(?:[ \\t]+#.*)?")''')
s=s.replace('''    if ":" in s:
        return s.find(":")
    return s.find("=")''','''    hits = [i for i in (s.find("="), s.find(":")) if i >= 0]
    return min(hits) if hits else -1''')
s=s.replace('s = line.strip()','s = line.strip(" \\t")').replace('key = s[:i].strip()','key = s[:i].strip(" \\t")')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git diff 2>/dev/null | head -5; grep -n 'SECTION =\|INCLUDE =\|strip\|hits' layercfg/lexer.py
cd /app && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -40; python tools/check.py
cd /app && rm -rf /tmp/o && python -m layercfg run --out /tmp/o && cat /tmp/o/errors.json; cat data/schema.json; ls data/shared
